sections.title: AI Is Opening New Doors. Are They Locked?
sections.intro: Traditional cyber security was not built for models that take instructions in plain English, remember what they are told and act on your systems. These are the gaps attackers already use.
items: Data leakage through AI tools
Staff paste customer details, contracts and pricing into public AI tools. Once it leaves your network, you lose control of it.
Prompt injection attacks
A hidden instruction in an email, PDF or web page can trick your chatbot or agent into revealing data or taking actions it should not.
Shadow AI
Teams sign up for AI apps without IT knowing. You cannot protect what you cannot see.
Over-permissioned AI agents
Agents connected to your inbox, CRM or ERP often get far more access than they need, turning one mistake into a breach.
Insecure AI integrations
API keys in code, unmonitored vector databases and third-party plugins create easy entry points.
Compliance exposure
New Privacy Act rules on automated decisions start in December 2026. AI that uses personal information without the right controls risks fines and lost trust.

faqs.question: What are AI security services?
faqs.answer: AI security services protect the AI tools, models and agents a business uses. They cover risks traditional cyber security misses, such as prompt injection, data leakage through AI tools, unsafe agent actions and AI privacy compliance.

faqs.question: Why do we need AI security if we already have cyber security?
faqs.answer: Standard cyber tools protect networks and devices. They do not stop a chatbot from being tricked into sharing customer data or an AI agent from acting outside its role. AI security adds controls built for how AI actually works.

faqs.question: Is AI regulated in Australia?
faqs.answer: Australia has no single AI law yet. Businesses must still meet the Privacy Act, Australian Consumer Law and industry rules when using AI. New Privacy Act transparency rules for automated decisions begin in December 2026.

faqs.question: What is prompt injection?
faqs.answer: Prompt injection is an attack where hidden instructions in a message, file or web page trick an AI system into ignoring its rules. It can lead to leaked data or unauthorised actions. We test for it and put guardrails in place to block it.

faqs.question: We only use ChatGPT or Copilot. Do we still need this?
faqs.answer: Yes. Everyday tools are where staff are most likely to paste sensitive data. An AI use policy, the right business settings and staff guidance can remove most of that risk quickly.

faqs.question: How much do AI security services cost?
faqs.answer: Cost depends on how many AI systems you run and how sensitive your data is. Your free assessment includes a clear quote with no surprises.

faqs.question: Do you work with businesses outside Melbourne?
faqs.answer: Yes. We are based in Melbourne and support businesses across Australia, including Sydney, Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, Canberra, Hobart, Darwin and the Gold Coast.

faqs.question: Can you secure AI inside our ERP?
faqs.answer: Yes. We implement and secure Odoo, SAP, Salesforce and Zoho, so we protect both the AI and the business data it connects to.
